title: Groupoïdes de Teichmüller et les S0 Tg,!ν, S0 TG : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, carried over from the previous pages. p: P → T is a quotient map by a free action of a group U, so T = P/U and p is a principal U-bundle. On each connected piece the homotopy sequence π = π_1(U,1) → π_1(P_i,x_i) → π_1(T_i,t_i) → 1 holds. When π → π_1(P_i,x_i) is surjective (or has a kernel N independent of i), the functor Π_1(p): Π_1(P) → Π_1(T) acquires what Grothendieck calls a 'π-structure': its fibres are banded by π (resp. by π' = π/N). In 'the preceding example' there is also a group homomorphism i_μ: μ → U, a μ-set ℰ, and a μ-equivariant map i_ℰ: ℰ → P (formula (7)).

This page.
(8) C' is the full sub-groupoid of Π_1(P) with object set ℰ, pulled back along i_ℰ: Hom_{C'}(x,y) = Hom_{Π_1(P)}(i_ℰ x, i_ℰ y). By transport of structure, μ acts on C' (μ acts on P through i_μ, hence on Π_1(P)), and C' → Π_1(P) is μ-equivariant.
(9) Passing to quotients gives i_{ℰ0}: ℰ_0 = ℰ/μ → T = P/U.
(10) C is the groupoid on ℰ_0 induced from Π_1(T) in the same way.
(11) This gives a commutative square of groupoids: C' → Π_1(P) across the top, C' → C (called f) on the left, Π_1(P) → Π_1(T) on the right, C → Π_1(T) across the bottom. The horizontal arrows are fully faithful by construction. The margin note says they are equivalences when the base-point set meets every connected component ('ℰ → Π_0(T) surjectif'). The square is μ-equivariant, with μ acting trivially on C and on Π_1(T) (continued on the next page).

Purpose (next page). Pull back the universal-cover extension 0 → π → Ũ → U → 0 along μ → U to get an extension 0 → π → ℰ̃ → μ → 0. Then, for x, y in one fibre C'_ξ with y = z·x, there is a canonical isomorphism of π-torsors Isom_{C'_ξ}(x,y) ≅ ℰ̃_z, under which composition corresponds to addition in ℰ̃. In other words, the π-structure on f: C' → C is computed explicitly from the extension class.

This is the familiar device of a fundamental groupoid on a well-chosen discrete set of base points, stable under a lattice-type group μ. It is used to give combinatorial or discrete models of Teichmüller groupoids: with U a torus-like group, π = π_1(U) ≅ Z^n generated by Dehn-twist-type loops, and the extension ℰ̃ encoding 'half-twists' or fractional twists.
errors: Minor gap. The top arrow C' → Π_1(P) is an equivalence iff ℰ → π_0(P) is surjective, and the bottom arrow iff ℰ_0 → π_0(T) is surjective. The margin states only 'ℰ → Π_0(T) surjectif'. That suffices for the bottom arrow, but for the top it implicitly needs π_0(P) ≅ π_0(T), e.g. U connected. The text is also cut off, so the condition is not fully stated.
The notation 'ℰ' is used both for the μ-set of base points and, on the next page, for the extension of μ by π. This is a notational clash, not a mathematical error.

ideas.what: Fundamental groupoid restricted to a chosen set of base points: the full subgroupoid induced along a map ℰ → P, which is an equivalence when ℰ meets all components
ideas.modern_name: fundamental groupoid on a set of base points Π_1(X,A)
ideas.usually_credited_to: R. Brown (1967-68); Grothendieck also uses it extensively
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), on Teichmüller groupoids with many base points; SGA1 for the algebraic fundamental groupoid

ideas.what: Equivariant transport of a group action to the induced groupoid, and the commutative square of induced groupoids over a principal U-bundle P → T
ideas.modern_name: fundamental groupoid of a principal bundle / quotient by a discrete group action; equivariant groupoid

ideas.what: π-structure on a functor of groupoids, i.e. fibres banded by π = π_1(U), described through the pullback of the universal-cover extension of U to μ (next page)
ideas.modern_name: groupoid fibration with abelian band / central extension of groupoids (a gerbe-like structure)

deep.surprise_reason: The page carries out routine groupoid bookkeeping: restricting fundamental groupoids to base-point sets, transporting the μ-action, and forming the commutative square of equivalences. It is a technical step in the unpublished Teichmüller-groupoid notes. The more interesting identification of fibres with an extension of μ by π_1(U) comes on the next page, and it too is standard.
transcription_corrections: The set written 'E' is a script ℰ throughout; ℰ_0 = ℰ/μ.
The phrase after (9) reads roughly 'soit C le groupoïde sur ℰ_0 comme ensemble d'objets induit par i_{ℰ0}'; a struck-out word precedes C.
Labels written on the arrows in (11), both on the top arrow and next to f, are crossed out; they look like 'equiv. ...' / 'surj. ...'.
Margin note: 'les flèches horizontales étant des équivalences, si ℰ → Π_0(T) surjectif ...'.
In (10) the objects are x_0, y_0 ∈ ℰ_0.
